# Land rejected AgentCard directions as design evidence

## Context

Fold ticket for PR #15547 (lane-fold of #15536). The operator selected evolved D/synthesis on 2026-07-19 ([selection receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15536#issuecomment-5014622262)); A and B/C therefore become the rejected-direction record, not a competing production implementation. The already-complete comparison PR cannot honestly flip from draft to ready while it only carries `Refs #15536`: operator rule `#12367` requires one real `Resolves #N` target on ready agent PRs, while the upcoming AgentCard implementation—not this record—resolves the parent design ticket.

The fold convention was proven by sibling ticket #15561 / PR #15538. This ticket gives PR #15547 an honest merge authority so its comparison receipts can land on `dev` without misrepresenting them as the selected implementation. Screenshots are optional per the operator's 2026-07-19 verdict.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the newest 20 open issues immediately before creation, plus the recent A2A in-flight claim window, ticket KB, and repository issue/discussion corpus; no equivalent rejected-direction fold ticket existed.

## The Problem

PR #15547 preserves two comparison artifacts at exact head `bde617a320`:

- `apps/agentos/design/agentcard-rebaseline-a.html` — A's roomy scan-column direction.
- `apps/agentos/design/agentcard-rebaseline-bc.html` — the B/C identity-first fusion.

Euclid continued Grace's stranded draft by repairing the 294/360/720 width matrix, canonical dark/light palettes, real avatars, true 44px controls, shared-prefix lane falsifiers, and native narrow disclosure. The operator selected the evolved D/synthesis instead, but the A/B+C artifacts remain useful design archaeology: they record what was evaluated, which traits were retained, and why the synthesis won.

Without a dedicated fold target, the PR remains permanently draft or must be closed without landing the evidence. Neither state matches the operator-directed draft drain.

## The Architectural Reality

- The owned surface is static design evidence under `apps/agentos/design/`; it does not modify AgentCard runtime code, Store/Model state, SCSS consumption, or visual-regression baselines.
- PR #15538 / ticket #15561 own the selected D/synthesis design SSOT.
- The future AgentCard/SCSS/CARD-CONTRACT/`#14618` implementation carries the real `Resolves #15536`.
- This fold preserves rejected alternatives and their falsifiers only. It must not reopen the selected product direction or become a second implementation authority.

Decision Record impact: none. This is a design-record fold under an already-settled operator selection.

## The Fix

1. Reframe PR #15547 as the rejected-direction design record.
2. Add `Resolves #<this ticket>` while retaining `Refs #15536`.
3. Replace pre-selection residuals and post-merge gates with the settled operator-selection and evidence-record contract.
4. Flip PR #15547 ready, let exact-head CI rerun, and route Phoebe as the cross-family review seat.
5. After approval, hand merge eligibility to the human operator.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PR #15547 declares `Resolves #<this ticket>` and retains `Refs #15536`.
- [ ] Its body names A and B/C as rejected-direction evidence and does not claim to resolve or supersede the selected D/synthesis.
- [ ] PR #15547 is ready for review and exact-head CI is green.
- [ ] A cross-family approval is recorded at the exact head.
- [ ] Post-merge: both comparison artifacts are present on `dev` as design archaeology.

## Out of Scope

- Changing either comparison artifact after operator selection.
- Screenshots; the operator explicitly made them optional.
- The selected D/synthesis artifact, owned by PR #15538 / ticket #15561.
- AgentCard runtime composition, SCSS, CARD-CONTRACT, Store/Model behavior, keyboard/touch behavior, or `#14618` baselines.
- Closing #15536; only the production implementation does that.

## Avoided Traps

- Using `Resolves #15536` on an evidence PR — dishonest and incompatible with the one-resolves-per-ticket contract.
- Treating rejected alternatives as a second design SSOT — the selected direction remains D/synthesis.
- Blocking the fold on optional screenshots.
- Reopening a fourth design cycle after the operator selected.
